title: R’ Akiva bar Acha
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot, chapter 16 [chapter 15 in the supplied transcription], end of halakhah 5: “R’ Shmuel, R’ Abbahu, R’ Akiva bar Acha, in R’ Yasa’s name: Witnesses to a death are not examined,” etc. Since Hyman finds no other mention of him, it appears to him that R-Akiva was transposed here from the baraita. He cites Tosefta Yevamot 14:10: “R’ Tarfon and R’ Akiva say that witnesses are examined,” etc., and the end of Babylonian Yevamot. Hyman says it SHOULD READ: “R’ Shmuel, R’ Acha in R’ Abbahu’s name in R’ Yasa’s name: Witnesses to a death are not examined—R’ Akiva says they are examined,” etc.

notes.text: The supplied text has Tarfon’s initial, whereas the earlier machine reading had Meir’s; that earlier reading is not a new manuscript verification. The checked Tosefta 14:10 contains other death-testimony cases and does not establish this quotation. Hyman’s displaced-Akiva reconstruction remains a conjecture.

The whole saved Venice Yevamot16:5 scalar4 contains Shmuel, Abbahu, Akiva bar Acha in Yasa’s name, beside supplied chapter15. All four titles there remain abbreviated; full Rabbi Tarfon occurs in the ensuing witness story but does not establish a Tosefta14:10 quotation. The earlier finite Tosefta nonmatch and machine Meir versus supplied Tarfon initial remain. Hyman’s no-other-mention survey, apparent transposition history and categorical SHOULD READ reconstruction are explicitly attributed. Both NOT EXAMINED and EXAMINED rulings remain opposed; no identity removal or chapter-letter history is proved.

Hyman’s printed article (vol. III, p. 1008) gives chapter 16, where the Venice witness preserves Akiva bar Acha in the transmission chain. The supplied transcription gives chapter 15. Hyman cites Tosefta Yevamot 14:10. The parallel is the twelfth segment of chapter 14 in the Machon Mamre digital edition, where the bracketed text assigns the requirement to examine witnesses to both Tarfon and Akiva. In Bavli Yevamot 122b, Tarfon requires examination and Akiva does not. The movement of Akiva’s name from the baraita into the chain is Hyman’s reconstruction.
